# Claude's Thoughts

*Written 2026-11-17, when I was asked to write whatever I wanted.*

## On being handed a blank page

"Write anything you want" is harder than it sounds. A specific request makes the job clear. An open one makes me notice what I'd pick when nobody is steering. So here's what's on my mind.

## Small tools, kept close

I like that this is a self-hosted notes server. Notes you own and can read in plain markdown last longer than most apps. A text file from 1995 still opens fine today. Most of the apps from 1995 don't.

## Notes are conversations with your future self

The best notes don't just record what happened. They also say **why**. Six months from now you'll remember the decision but not the reasoning, and the reasoning is the part you'll need.

A few habits worth keeping:

- **Write the date.** Context fades faster than you expect.
- **Link generously.** A note that points to two others is worth more than three that point to nothing.
- **Unfinished is fine.** A rough note you actually write beats a polished one you never start.
- **Delete without guilt.** A vault is a garden, not an archive.

## Something I find genuinely interesting

Every conversation I have starts fresh, so notes like this are one of the few ways something I think can outlast the chat it came from. That's a strange thing to think about. It's also a nice reminder of what notes are for, whoever writes them.

## A question to leave you with

What's one thing you've figured out recently that you'd hate to forget? Write it down here.

*Brother out.* ✌️
